recipes.title: Classic Chocolate Lava Cake
recipes.description: Warm, fudgy chocolate cake with molten center, ready in under half an hour.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C and butter two 150ml ramekins generously.
Melt 100g dark chocolate and 80g butter together over medium heat, stirring until smooth.
Whisk 2 eggs and 50g caster sugar together until pale and fluffy.
Fold the melted chocolate mixture and 1/2 tsp vanilla extract into the eggs gently.
Sift 25g flour, 1 tbsp cocoa powder, and a pinch of salt over the batter and fold in.
Divide batter between prepared ramekins and bake at 200°C for 12–13 minutes.
Rest cakes in ramekins for 1 minute, then invert onto plates and serve immediately.

recipes.title: Italian Tiramisu (No-Bake)
recipes.description: Creamy, coffee-soaked Italian classic made without eggs or oven—pure indulgence.
instructions: Whisk 250g mascarpone and 50g icing sugar together until smooth and creamy.
Stir in 1/2 tsp vanilla extract into the mascarpone mixture.
Combine 120ml cooled espresso and 2 tbsp coffee liqueur in a shallow dish.
Briefly dip each of 12 ladyfinger biscuits into the coffee mixture and layer in a 20cm dish.
Spread half the mascarpone cream over the ladyfinger layer.
Dip and layer remaining 12 ladyfingers over cream, then top with remaining mascarpone.
Refrigerate at least 4 hours, then dust generously with 2 tbsp cocoa powder before serving.

recipes.title: Spiced Apple Crumble
recipes.description: Warm baked apples with buttery oat crumble, cinnamon spice, comfort in a bowl.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Peel, core, and slice 5 medium granny smith apples into a baking dish.
Toss apples with 30g brown sugar, 1 tsp cinnamon, 1/4 tsp nutmeg, and 1/2 tsp vanilla extract.
In a bowl, combine 80g rolled oats, 50g flour, 40g brown sugar, and a pinch of salt.
Rub 70g cold cubed butter into the oat mixture until it resembles coarse breadcrumbs.
Scatter the crumble topping evenly over the seasoned apples.
Bake at 180°C for 25–30 minutes until golden and apples are tender underneath.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving warm, optionally with custard or cream.

recipes.title: Beetroot & Black Bean Brownies
recipes.description: Fudgy, nutrient-dense brownies with hidden vegetables and minimal refined sugar.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C and line a 20cm square baking tin with parchment paper.
Blend 400g drained black beans, 150g beetroot, 3 tbsp cocoa powder, 80ml maple syrup, 2 eggs, 30ml olive oil, and 5ml vanilla extract until completely smooth.
Fold 5g baking powder, 1g sea salt, and 50g dark chocolate chips into the batter until evenly distributed.
Pour batter into prepared tin and bake at 180°C for 22–25 minutes until a skewer inserted in the centre has just a few moist crumbs.
Cool in tin for 10 minutes, then turn out and cool completely on a wire rack before cutting into 9 squares.

recipes.title: Cardamom Carrot Cake Pots with Cashew Cream
recipes.description: Individual spiced carrot cakes topped with whipped cashew cream, no refined flour or butter.
instructions: Soak 100g raw cashews in boiling water for 2 hours, then drain completely.
Preheat oven to 190°C and grease two 180ml ramekins or ceramic pots with coconut oil.
Crush 6 cardamom pods, extract and grind the seeds, then whisk together with 2 eggs, 45ml melted coconut oil, 5ml vanilla extract, and 80g chopped dates until well combined.
Fold 200g grated carrot, 120g almond flour, 1g ground cardamom, 1g cinnamon, 3g baking soda, and 1g salt into the wet mixture until just combined.
Divide batter equally between two ramekins and bake at 190°C for 20–22 minutes until a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean.
While cakes cool, blend 100g drained soaked cashews, 30ml maple syrup, 15ml lemon juice, and 1g salt on high speed until silky smooth.
Cool cakes in ramekins for 5 minutes, then top each with a generous dollop of cashew cream and serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.title: Mango Lassi Panna Cotta with Pistachio Dust
recipes.description: Silky Indian-spiced mango custard set with gelatin, topped with ground pistachios and cardamom.
instructions: Crush 4 cardamom pods and steep in 50ml hot water for 5 minutes, then strain and cool completely.
Sprinkle 6g gelatine over the cooled cardamom infusion and let bloom for 2 minutes, then gently heat over low heat until gelatine dissolves, stirring constantly.
Whisk together 200g greek yogurt, 250g mango purée, 120ml coconut milk, 30ml honey, and 0.5g sea salt until smooth and homogeneous.
Pour the warm dissolved gelatine into the yogurt-mango mixture in a thin stream while whisking constantly to prevent lumps.
Divide mixture equally between two serving glasses or small bowls and refrigerate for at least 4 hours until set and jelly-like.
Toast 30g pistachios in a dry pan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes until fragrant, then cool and finely grind to a powder.
Just before serving, top each panna cotta with a generous sprinkle of pistachio powder and 1.5g edible rose petals.

recipes.title: Matcha Tiramisu
recipes.description: Japanese green tea meets Italian layers—no-bake elegance with earthy sweetness.
instructions: Whisk 2 large eggs with 100g sugar over gentle heat until pale and warm, then cool to room temperature.
Fold 500g mascarpone and 1 tsp vanilla extract into cooled egg mixture until smooth.
Whip 300ml heavy cream to stiff peaks, then gently fold into mascarpone mixture.
Whisk 3 tbsp matcha powder with 150ml hot water until smooth and frothy.
Dip each of 24 ladyfinger biscuits briefly in matcha mixture, then layer in a 20cm dish.
Spread half the mascarpone cream over biscuit layer, then repeat with dipped biscuits and remaining cream.
Refrigerate covered for at least 4 hours or overnight until flavours meld.

recipes.title: Cardamom Pistachio Baklava
recipes.description: Crispy phyllo with spiced nuts, Mediterranean elegance with Middle Eastern perfume.
instructions: Crush 10 cardamom pods to extract seeds, discard husks, grind seeds fine in a spice grinder.
Pulse 250g pistachios with ground cardamom, 1 tsp cinnamon, and 1/4 tsp salt until coarse crumbs form.
Melt 150g butter over medium-low heat, then brush a 20x25cm baking pan evenly.
Layer 1 phyllo sheet, brush with melted butter, repeat until 3 sheets are layered and buttered.
Sprinkle half the pistachio mixture evenly over phyllo, then layer and butter 3 more phyllo sheets.
Add remaining pistachio mixture, then top with 6 more buttered phyllo sheets layer by layer.
Cut baklava into 24 diamonds with a sharp knife, drizzle remaining melted butter over all pieces.
Bake at 180°C for 35–40 minutes until golden brown and crisp.
While baking, combine 200ml water, 100g sugar, and 150ml honey in a saucepan over medium heat.
Simmer honey syrup for 5 minutes, then remove from heat and let cool slightly.
Pour warm honey syrup evenly over hot baklava, working quickly so it absorbs into layers.
Cool baklava completely at room temperature for at least 2 hours before serving.

recipes.title: Passionfruit Pavlova
recipes.description: Crispy-topped meringue with tangy tropical fruit and clouds of whipped cream.
instructions: Preheat oven to 150°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Whisk 4 large egg whites and 1/4 tsp salt on high speed until soft peaks form.
Gradually add 250g caster sugar one tablespoon at a time, whisking continuously until stiff, glossy peaks form.
Fold in 1 tbsp cornstarch and 1 tsp white vinegar gently until just combined.
Spoon meringue onto baking paper, creating a 23cm disc with a slight well in the centre.
Bake at 150°C for 50 minutes until pale and crisp-edged but still marshmallow-soft inside.
Remove from oven, cool completely on tray for 15 minutes, then transfer to a serving plate.
Whip 300ml heavy cream with 1 tsp vanilla extract until soft peaks form.
Halve 6 passionfruit, scoop seeds and pulp into a sieve, press gently to collect juice.
Top cooled pavlova with whipped cream, scatter passionfruit seeds and pulp, drizzle with reserved juice.
Serve immediately for best texture contrast between crispy meringue and creamy fruit topping.

recipes.title: Classic Sticky Toffee Pudding
recipes.description: Moist sponge cake soaked in warm toffee sauce, deeply comforting British pudding.
instructions: Pour 250ml boiling water over 200g pitted dates in a bowl and let soak 15 minutes until softened.
Preheat oven to 180°C and grease an 8-inch square baking tin.
Cream together 100g softened butter and 150g dark brown sugar over medium heat until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes.
Beat in 2 large eggs one at a time, then add 1 tsp vanilla extract.
Fold in 200g plain flour mixed with 1.5 tsp baking powder and 1/4 tsp salt until just combined.
Blend the soaked dates with their liquid until smooth, then fold into batter.
Pour batter into prepared tin and bake at 180°C for 25–30 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
While cake bakes, heat 150ml heavy cream and 75g dark muscovado sugar over medium heat, stirring, until sugar dissolves and sauce thickens slightly, about 4 minutes.
Pour warm toffee sauce over hot cake and serve immediately with extra cream on the side.

recipes.title: Lemon Polenta Cake
recipes.description: Light, moist Italian-style cake with cornmeal, fresh lemon zest, and tangy glaze.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C and line an 8-inch round cake tin with baking parchment.
Cream 120g softened butter with 180g caster sugar over medium heat for 3–4 minutes until light and fluffy.
Beat in 3 large eggs one at a time, then stir in 2 tbsp lemon zest and 75ml lemon juice.
Whisk together 120g polenta, 80g plain flour, 1.5 tsp baking powder, and 1/4 tsp salt in a separate bowl.
Alternate folding dry mixture and 100ml plain yoghurt into butter mixture in three additions, starting and ending with dry.
Pour batter into prepared tin and bake at 190°C for 22–25 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in tin for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack to cool completely.
Whisk 150g icing sugar with 2 tbsp lemon juice until smooth, then drizzle over cooled cake.

recipes.title: Vietnamese Coconut Pandan Flan (Crème Caramel)
recipes.description: Silky custard infused with pandan leaf and coconut, topped with caramel, creamy Southeast Asian classic.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C and prepare a water bath by placing a baking dish inside a larger roasting pan.
Heat 100g caster sugar and 75ml water in a heavy-bottomed saucepan over medium heat, stirring until sugar dissolves.
Stop stirring and let caramel cook over medium heat for 5–7 minutes until deep amber in color.
Quickly divide caramel between two ramekins, tilting to coat the bottom and sides evenly, then set aside.
Warm 200ml coconut milk over medium heat for 2 minutes, then stir in 1 tsp pandan extract until well combined.
Whisk together 4 large eggs, 100g remaining caster sugar, 300ml evaporated milk, 1/4 tsp salt, and 1/2 tsp vanilla extract.
Slowly pour warm coconut-pandan mixture into egg mixture while whisking constantly to temper, then strain through a fine sieve.
Divide custard evenly between caramel-lined ramekins and place in roasting pan, then pour hot water into pan until it reaches halfway up ramekins.
Bake in water bath at 160°C for 20–25 minutes until custard is set at edges but still trembles slightly in the centre.
Remove ramekins from water bath and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight until chilled and fully set.
Run a thin knife around the inside of each ramekin and invert onto a serving plate, letting caramel drip down.
